text: Usually we create this kind of networks. Okay, so that's done. Let me just mention something about the mobility. Right, that was the other criterion that we introduced. What kind of mobility is supported by our networks? Well, when we have Wi-Fi, typically the mobility that is supported is the nomadic mobility. That is users move from one place to another, then stay for a while in a place, then they move again and so on. This is called nomadic mobility, and it is the typical mobility pattern of Wi-Fi users. Like us, we come to campus, we stay here for a while, and then we go for lunch to the canteen, and then we stay there, and then move again and so on. For cellular networks, well, of course, we may support nomadic mobility, but cellular networks are very very good also in supporting high speed mobility. So vehicles that move on the streets, we may have also trains, high speed trains. The train itself may have cellular connectivity with the with the internet. So in general, cellular networks are extremely good in providing high quality service to.
